chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim ibn Abbas narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Abu Qutada al-Harrani narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Zadhan, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

When Allah — Mighty and Majestic — opened Mecca, we set out, and we were eight thousand men. When evening came upon us, we had become ten thousand Muslims. So emigration was lifted, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no emigration after the conquest of Mecca.'

Then we arrived at Hawazin, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Stand and behold your honour with Allah, Mighty and Majestic — speak to the Sun when it rises.'
Ibn Abbas said: By Allah, I did not envy anyone except Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) on that day. I said to al-Fadl: 'Come, let us see how Ali ibn Abi Talib speaks to the Sun.'

When the Sun rose, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) stood and said: 'Peace be upon you, O righteous, obedient servant — perpetually in the obedience of Allah, your Lord.' The Sun replied to him, saying: 'And upon you be peace, O brother of the Messenger of Allah, his vicegerent, and the Proof of Allah over His creation.'

Then Ali (peace be upon him) fell prostrate in gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: By Allah, I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stand and take Ali (peace be upon him) by the head, helping him rise and wiping his face, saying: 'Rise, my beloved, for you have made the people of heaven weep by your weeping, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has boasted about you to the carriers of His Throne.'

key_terms.الْهِجْرَة: Emigration — the religious obligation of migrating from Mecca to Medina, which was lifted after the conquest
key_terms.حَمَلَة الْعَرْش: Carriers of the Throne — the exalted angels who bear the divine Throne
key_terms.حُجَّة: Proof, argument — one whose existence and qualities are a divine proof over creation
key_terms.كَرَامَة: Divine honour, spiritual distinction — an elevated status bestowed by God upon His chosen servants
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Vicegerent, executor — the designated successor and deputy of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about Ali ibn Abi Talib speaking to the Sun after the conquest of Mecca?
ai.summary: Ibn Abbas narrates a miraculous event at the Battle of Hunayn, shortly after the conquest of Mecca. The Prophet commanded Ali ibn Abi Talib to speak to the rising Sun as a demonstration of his divine honour, and the Sun miraculously responded, addressing Ali as the brother of the Prophet, his vicegerent, and the Proof of Allah. The hadith culminates with the Prophet tenderly raising the prostrated, weeping Ali and informing him that God had boasted about him to the angels bearing the Throne.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim b. `Abbas narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Abu Qutada al-Harrani narrated to us from Ja`far b. Burqan from Maymun b. Mahran from Zadhan from Ibn `Abbas. He said:

When Allah liberated Mecca, we went out, and we had eight thousand men; and when we entered the evening, we had ten thousand Muslims. So, emigration was mentioned, and the Messenger of Allah (s) said: There is no emigration after the conquest of Mecca.
He said: Then, we ended up in Hawazin, and the Prophet (s) said to `Ali b. Abi Talib (as): O `Ali! Stand, and look to your honour with Allah. Speak to the Sun once it rises.
Ibn `Abbas said: By Allah, I did not envy anyone except `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) on that day. So, I said to Fadl: Stand up so that we may see how `Ali b. Abi Talib speaks to the Sun.

So, when the Sun rose, `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) stood and said: Peace be unto you – O perpetual, obedient, and righteous servant – in the obedience of Allah, its Lord. So, the Sun replied to him, saying: And also with you, O brother and deputy of the Messenger of Allah, O Proof of Allah over His creation.

So, `Ali (as) fell [weeping] in a prostration of gratitude toward Allah. He said: By Allah, I saw the Messenger of Allah (s) stand, take `Ali (as) by the head, help him stand up, and wipe his face, saying: Stand, my beloved, for you have made the people of heaven weep from your weeping. Allah has boasted to the carriers of the Throne about you.
